cs.t: After my AllClad pans have started to get the sharp edges from dishwasher corrosion of the aluminum layer, I've been switching to Hestan Nanobond.  It's not exactly nonstick, but the surface is so hard and polished that things don't stick very much and you can use metal implements without scratching the pan. But I think AllClad has switched to sealed-rims on their pans, thus making them truly dishwasher-safe?
cs.th: Cookware Got Worse on Purpose: Who Owns Pyrex and All-Clad Now

cs.t: Thank you for these tests! I've recently tossed all my coated pans (my favourite were the Anolon, but those too shed) and moved to stainless steel, save for a cast iron and carbon steel pan. In the journey here the best I could find was a Hestan nanobond pan, which unfortunately laminated and has shown some pits after few months of use. They refunded me but titaniums isn't yet where stainless steel is. Now I'm using a mix of Demeyere, De Buyer, and Made In. It takes a bit of time to get used cooking in them without a ton of fat. Look up Leidenfrost effect on youtube and you'll learn pretty quickly how to use stainless steel and do not let anything stick even fish.
cs.th: We Tested Nonstick Cookware: Coatings Don't Need to Look Worn to Shed Particles
